data.name: Grimtale Island
data.detailed_description:
Grimtale Island is an open world survival game set in a beautiful low poly art style.

Explore and master survival on a island that has been taken over by a strange infection causing the dead to return to the world of the living.
Craft gather and build to stay alive in this world.

OPEN WORLD

Explore a beautiful Dynamic open world set on multiple Islands.

VEHICLES

Explore the world using the 3 vehicles provided. (helicopter, Humvee and Lav puma)

DAY AND NIGHT CYCLE

A full 20 min day and 20 min night cycle.

DYNAMIC WEATHER PATTERNS

Fully Dynamic weather and season patterns. (Snow,Rain,Thunder) (Winter,Summer,Fall) Watch the world change in front of your eyes!.

WORLD TEMPERATURE

Craft a fire to stay warm in the cold temperatures.

HUNTING

Hunt animals to harvest meat to survive.

CRAFTING

Craft tools, weapons and Resources to survive, gather and fight of the dead.

FARMING

Grow crops to become a master of survival.

LOOTING

Enter abandoned buildings and scavange through the old world to find items of use.

BASE BUILDING

Build a place to come home to after a long day of looting and slaying the dead.

TRADE AND SELL

Find Trader Bots around the island. Sell your unwanted loot and buy new loot.

reviews.review:
Grimtale Island is an independently developed open-world survival game that combines zombie encounters with exploration, resource management, crafting, construction, and environmental hazards. Developed and published by Michael Schade, the game uses a colorful low-poly visual style rather than pursuing the grim realism commonly associated with post-apocalyptic survival games. The premise revolves around a mysterious infection that has overtaken a collection of islands and caused the dead to return to life. Players are dropped into this dangerous environment and expected to gather supplies, create equipment, establish shelter, and gradually learn how to survive.

Exploration is central to the experience, with the world extending across multiple islands rather than remaining confined to one small location. Abandoned buildings provide opportunities to search through the remnants of civilization for useful equipment and resources. This scavenging system gives players a practical reason to leave the relative security of their base. Every journey into unfamiliar territory can potentially provide materials necessary for crafting, food, weapons, or items that can be exchanged later. The open-world design consequently supports the game's broader survival loop by constantly encouraging movement and discovery.

Transportation makes traveling across the environment more interesting. Grimtale Island provides three vehicles: a Humvee, LAV Puma, and helicopter. Each offers a different way of navigating the world, while the helicopter is particularly useful for giving exploration a greater sense of freedom. Vehicles also fit naturally into the abandoned-world setting, making them more than simple conveniences. Finding ways to travel efficiently becomes increasingly valuable when gathering resources and returning from distant expeditions.

The environment itself plays an active role in survival. Grimtale Island features twenty-minute daytime and nighttime periods alongside changing weather conditions such as rain, snow, and thunderstorms. Seasonal changes include summer, fall, and winter, helping the landscape feel less static over extended play sessions. Temperature also has gameplay consequences. Cold conditions require players to create fires to remain warm, meaning weather is not entirely cosmetic. These systems provide additional considerations beyond simply watching for zombies.

Resource management expands through hunting, farming, and crafting. Animals can be hunted for meat, providing an immediate method of obtaining food, while crops offer a more sustainable option once players establish themselves. Crafting allows collected resources to become tools and weapons needed for gathering materials and defending against the undead. The interaction between these mechanics gives progression a satisfying survival-oriented structure. Initially, players may depend heavily on scavenging and hunting, while farming and base construction represent a transition toward greater stability.

Base building is especially important because it gives collected materials a lasting purpose. Constructing a home creates a destination to return to after exploring, fighting, and looting. Instead of endlessly wandering without meaningful attachment to the environment, players can develop their own safe area and use it as the center of future expeditions. The concept works well with the game's scavenging emphasis because successful trips provide tangible improvements to the player's ability to survive.

Trading adds another useful dimension. Trader Bots located around the islands allow unwanted loot to be sold and replacement items to be purchased. This means equipment that is not immediately useful can still contribute toward progression. It also makes discovering traders valuable during exploration and provides an alternative to obtaining everything through crafting or random scavenging. Hunting, farming, looting, trading, crafting, and construction collectively provide several interconnected ways to develop rather than forcing every player into one repetitive activity.

Combat with the undead provides the constant threat tying these mechanics together. However, Grimtale Island is not designed solely as a zombie shooter. Survival remains the larger objective, with fighting serving alongside environmental management and resource collection rather than replacing them. This approach gives the game more variety, particularly for players who prefer gradually establishing themselves in a hostile sandbox instead of moving through a strictly linear series of combat encounters.

The low-poly presentation complements the modest scale of the project. It gives Grimtale Island a recognizable appearance while keeping the environments readable and allowing weather and seasonal changes to alter the atmosphere noticeably. The game also has relatively modest hardware requirements and occupies only a small amount of storage space. Its visual simplicity should therefore be viewed as part of its identity rather than as an attempt to compete with technically elaborate modern survival productions.

The main weakness is that Grimtale Island attempts to cover an enormous range of mechanics for a small independent project. Vehicles, weather, seasons, temperature, zombies, hunting, farming, crafting, trading, looting, exploration, and base construction create an ambitious feature list, but players expecting each component to possess the depth of a specialized survival game may find the individual systems comparatively straightforward. Its mixed Steam reception also suggests that the execution will not appeal equally to everyone. Players who prioritize refinement and complex simulation may therefore be less impressed than those who simply enjoy experimenting with accessible survival sandboxes.

Overall, Grimtale Island is an interesting survival experiment built around breadth rather than exceptional complexity in any single area. Michael Schade's work as both developer and publisher results in a game with the unmistakable character of a personal independent project. Its combination of infected islands, scavenging, vehicles, environmental hazards, crafting, farming, hunting, trading, and construction provides plenty of activities within a compact free-to-play package. It may lack the sophistication and polish of larger survival games, but its broad collection of mechanics and distinctive low-poly setting give it enough personality to be worth investigating for dedicated fans of the genre.

Rating: 6/10
